owner: W1-05 — roads, signposts and getting there without a marker
note: The eight road topics, one per settlement, so that `the road to Gideon` is a keyword the province actually holds rather than a string invented at runtime. Seam S35 permits a map and confines it to ground already walked, which means that on a first journey the map is blank ahead of you and these words are how you get anywhere; RI-WLD06 L3 makes the spoken direction the third wayfinding layer under the road itself and the signposts on it. The LOCATED answers — the ones that actually take you somewhere, keyed to the settlement you are standing in and to who you asked — are not here. They live in `game/data/dialogue/road-directions.json` and are supplied by `RoadBook` in `game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js`, which wins in `Conversation.say()` because `extra` is consulted before the topic index. What is here is the OTHER case, and it is the common one: you asked somebody who does not walk that road. A woman in Lilmoth asked about the Stormhold road has an opinion about Stormhold and no directions to it, and saying so out loud is a better answer than silence — the same reasoning `world/opacity.json` is built on. Every place named in these infos is a record in `game/data/world/pois.json` or a settlement in `game/data/world/settlements/`; `tools/world/signpost-audit.mjs` checks that and fails if one dangles.

infos.x: Gideon's where the paving stops being ours and starts being theirs. If you're not standing in Helstrom, you're not on the road to it, whatever anyone tells you. So get to Helstrom, find the milepost outside the west gate, and walk until the stone runs out.

Everything I sell that came off a wheel came through Gideon. The road is west out of Helstrom and it is the only one in this province a cart survives. Have you priced anything since you got here? Now you know.

Not from here you don't. Gideon sits off the west edge of everything I know. Have you been to Helstrom? Ask there — they are on the Legion road and they will point you the right way without charging you for it.

Helstrom is where the roads agree to meet, and it is the only place in the province where that is true. Whatever corner you are in, there is a way to it, and if you keep asking as you go you will be handed along from one person to the next until you are standing in the Stone Forest looking up.
Everything goes to Helstrom eventually. Water does. So do you, if you walk long enough and don't go into the water first.
Inland and up. That is as much as I can give you standing here. A traveller on the road itself will do better — they always do.

Blackrose is a prison with a town grown round it, and the road to it isn't a road. It's a trail through standing water. We don't maintain it and we don't recommend it. But if you must, go south out of Helstrom, and go in daylight.
People come back from Blackrose with their feet in a state I can do very little about. Are you set on going? Then wherever you pick the trail up, don't pick it up at dusk.
South, but not from here. You want a Helstrom man or a Lilmoth man for that — both have a way to it and both ways are wet.

You'll smell Lilmoth a good while before you see it, and once you're near the coast you can't really miss it. It's the only thing on that shore big enough to be called anything. Do you know how you're getting to the coast? The coast is the hard part. Lilmoth is easy once you are on it.

South and south and then further south than you think, until the ground stops pretending. I have made that journey more times than I would choose to and it has never once been shorter than I remembered.
Downriver, in the end. Everything is downriver of here. Ask on the coast road — anyone walking it is going to Lilmoth or coming from it, there is nothing else down there.

Archon keeps to itself in the Deep Marshes, and the ways to it are ways, not roads. There's no stone on any of them. Whoever takes you in will tell you the turns. They aren't written down, because writing them down has never once helped.
Archon. Now that's a place a man can be left alone in. You won't find it from here. You find it from Thorn, or from the Lilmoth track, if you've the stomach for the Lilmoth track.
Into the marsh proper, and I have never been. Ask at Thorn. They are close enough to it to have an honest answer.

Thorn sits on the far side of the moor from most things, and the moor is what makes it hard, not the distance. Whoever sends you should send you with the turns, because the ground up there gives you nothing to steer by for a long stretch.
Thorn pays late and pays anyway. You come at it off the Stormhold track or up from Archon, and both of those you want to be walking in the morning, not the afternoon.
North and east of everything down here. Not a walk you start from this town. Stormhold has the track to it.
Stormhold's a garrison, and it's where the province stops being a guess. The way there is signed at every junction that matters, which isn't many junctions. But they're the right ones.
Half the people who drink here are on their way to Stormhold or have just come from it and are still complaining. Why ask me? Ask one of them. They will be delighted to be asked.
North. A long way north, and I couldn't tell you the turns. Whoever put you on the road at all will know them better than I do.
Soulrest is on the water, and it's quiet in a way that people who aren't from there find unpleasant. You come to it along the shore. There's no other way and there never was.
Soulrest is older than the road to it. Does that surprise you? It should not. A great deal here is older than the way people get to it.
The coast. That is honestly all I have. Gideon or Blackrose will do you better — both of them look out that way.
